meta.description: One-sentence historical definitions for Newport street directory occupations (1876-1936).

labourer.title: Labourer
labourer.summary: A general manual worker employed on docks, building sites, railways, or municipal works without a single fixed trade.

dock labourer.title: Dock Labourer
dock labourer.summary: A waterside worker loading and unloading timber, iron, pitwood, and general cargo at Newport's Alexandra and Town Docks.

ironworker.title: Ironworker
ironworker.summary: A skilled or semi-skilled foundry or rolling-mill hand shaping, forging, or finishing wrought and cast iron.

steelworker.title: Steelworker
steelworker.summary: A heavy-industry worker employed at Newport's steelworks and sheet mills, such as Lysaght's Orb Works.

carpenter.title: Carpenter
carpenter.summary: A woodworker framing roofs, floors, staircases, and structural timberwork in houses and dockside buildings.

joiner.title: Joiner
joiner.summary: A fine woodworker crafting doors, window sashes, staircases, and interior fittings in a workshop.

cabinetmaker.title: Cabinetmaker
cabinetmaker.summary: A specialist furniture maker building tables, chests, sideboards, and shop fittings.

void.title: Void
void.summary: A directory notation indicating the property was unoccupied or between tenants when the volume was compiled.

vacant sites.title: Vacant Sites
vacant sites.summary: Undeveloped building plots along a newly laid-out street awaiting residential or commercial construction.

g.w.r..title: G.W.R. (Great Western Railway)
g.w.r..summary: An employee of the Great Western Railway, which operated Newport's main passenger lines, goods yards, and coal sidings.

mason.title: Mason
mason.summary: A stonecutter and wall-builder working dressed stone and rubble for Newport's Victorian terraces, churches, and docks.

fitter.title: Fitter
fitter.summary: A mechanical engineer assembling, adjusting, and repairing engines, locomotives, marine machinery, or pipework.

signal fitter.title: Signal Fitter
signal fitter.summary: A railway technician installing and maintaining mechanical semaphore signals, points, and interlocking levers.

coal trimmer.title: Coal Trimmer
coal trimmer.summary: A specialist dockworker who levelled and packed coal inside ships' holds so vessels remained stable at sea.

trimmer.title: Trimmer
trimmer.summary: A dock or steamship worker trimming coal bunkers and cargo holds for safe vessel balance.

coal shipper.title: Coal Shipper
coal shipper.summary: A merchant or dock agent arranging the export and loading of South Wales steam coal onto cargo ships.

coal merchant.title: Coal Merchant
coal merchant.summary: A wholesale or retail dealer supplying house coal, coke, and industrial fuel from wharf or railway depots.

clerk.title: Clerk
clerk.summary: An office worker keeping ledgers, correspondence, shipping manifests, or railway accounts.

engine driver.title: Engine Driver
engine driver.summary: An operator of a steam locomotive, stationary winding engine, or dockside steam plant.

engineman.title: Engineman
engineman.summary: A technician tending and firing stationary steam engines at docks, factories, or pumping stations.

haulier.title: Haulier
haulier.summary: A horse-and-cart or motor carrier transporting coal, building materials, timber, and goods across town.

carman.title: Carman
carman.summary: A driver of a horse-drawn delivery cart or railway goods van.

painter.title: Painter
painter.summary: A house or ship painter applying protective coatings, lettering, and interior finishes.

decorator.title: Decorator
decorator.summary: A tradesman specialising in interior wallpapering, graining, marbling, and ornamental paintwork.

grocer.title: Grocer
grocer.summary: A neighbourhood shopkeeper selling tea, sugar, flour, dried goods, and household provisions.

butcher.title: Butcher
butcher.summary: A meat retailer dressing and selling fresh beef, lamb, and mutton from a street shop or market stall.

pork butcher.title: Pork Butcher
pork butcher.summary: A specialist butcher curing bacon, hams, sausages, and cooked meats.

seaman.title: Seaman
seaman.summary: A merchant sailor crewing coastal or ocean-going steamships and sailing vessels out of Newport.

mariner.title: Mariner
mariner.summary: A qualified sea-going sailor or deckhand serving on merchant vessels.

master mariner.title: Master Mariner
master mariner.summary: A certificated ship's captain qualified to command merchant vessels on deep-sea or coastal voyages.

sailor.title: Sailor
sailor.summary: A deckhand aboard merchant or coastal vessels trading through the Bristol Channel.

tailor.title: Tailor
tailor.summary: A garment maker cutting, fitting, and sewing men's suits, coats, and uniforms to order.

engineer.title: Engineer
engineer.summary: A mechanical, civil, or marine engineer designing, building, or maintaining engines and industrial plant.

marine engineer.title: Marine Engineer
marine engineer.summary: A shipboard or dockyard engineer responsible for steamship boilers, propulsion engines, and auxiliary machinery.

smith.title: Smith
smith.summary: A metalworker forging iron tools, chains, hinges, and fittings at a heated hearth and anvil.

blacksmith.title: Blacksmith
blacksmith.summary: A heavy iron smith shoeing horses and forging ironwork for carts, ships, and construction.

striker.title: Striker
striker.summary: A blacksmith's assistant wielding a heavy sledgehammer on the anvil in rhythm with the master smith.

plasterer.title: Plasterer
plasterer.summary: A building tradesman applying lime mortar, lath-and-plaster walls, and decorative ceiling cornices.

guard.title: Guard
guard.summary: A railway official in charge of a passenger or freight train's safety, braking, and timetable.

boilermaker.title: Boilermaker
boilermaker.summary: A skilled metalworker fabricating and riveting high-pressure steam boilers for locomotives, ships, and factories.

moulder.title: Moulder
moulder.summary: A foundry craftsman packing sand moulds into which molten iron or brass was poured to make castings.

baker.title: Baker
baker.summary: A bread and pastry maker firing daily loaves in brick ovens for neighbourhood customers.

confectioner.title: Confectioner
confectioner.summary: A maker and seller of cakes, pastries, sugar sweets, and light refreshments.

foreman.title: Foreman
foreman.summary: A senior chargehand supervising crews on the docks, railways, building sites, or factory floors.

gardener.title: Gardener
gardener.summary: A domestic or market gardener tending private grounds, nurseries, or municipal parks.

shop.title: Shop
shop.summary: A general neighbourhood retail shop, often run from the front room of a terraced house.

general shop.title: General Shop
general shop.summary: A small corner store stocking everyday groceries, bread, candles, and household sundries.

shopkeeper.title: Shopkeeper
shopkeeper.summary: The proprietor of a local retail shop.

greengrocer.title: Greengrocer
greengrocer.summary: A retailer of fresh vegetables, fruit, and potatoes.

fruiterer.title: Fruiterer
fruiterer.summary: A shopkeeper or market stallholder specialising in fresh and dried fruit.

fireman.title: Fireman
fireman.summary: A stoker shovelling coal into the firebox of a railway locomotive, steamship boiler, or stationary engine.

stoker.title: Stoker
stoker.summary: A worker tending furnaces and steam boilers in ships, gasworks, or industrial plants.

traveller.title: Traveller
traveller.summary: A commercial travelling salesman taking wholesale orders for manufacturers across South Wales.

commercial traveller.title: Commercial Traveller
commercial traveller.summary: A wholesale sales representative visiting retail shops across the region with trade samples.

bootmaker.title: Bootmaker
bootmaker.summary: A craftsman making and repairing leather boots and work footwear.

shoemaker.title: Shoemaker
shoemaker.summary: A cordwainer or cobbler crafting and mending leather shoes.

hairdresser.title: Hairdresser
hairdresser.summary: A barber or ladies' hairdresser cutting hair, shaving, and selling perfumery.

builder.title: Builder
builder.summary: A building contractor undertaking house, shop, and civic construction.

widow.title: Widow
widow.summary: A female head of household recorded by marital status rather than a separate paid occupation.

manager.title: Manager
manager.summary: A salaried supervisor running a shop, bank branch, works department, or hotel.

manageress.title: Manageress
manageress.summary: A woman managing a shop, refreshment room, hotel, or business department.

bricklayer.title: Bricklayer
bricklayer.summary: A tradesman laying kiln bricks and mortar for houses, chimneys, and industrial walls.

signalman.title: Signalman
signalman.summary: A railway operator working levers in a signal box to route trains safely across junctions.

platelayer.title: Platelayer
platelayer.summary: A railway trackman laying, packing, and maintaining rails, sleepers, and ballast.

shunter.title: Shunter
shunter.summary: A railyard worker coupling, uncoupling, and marshalling coal wagons and goods trains.

porter.title: Porter
porter.summary: A station, hotel, or warehouse worker carrying luggage, parcels, and freight.

blacksmith.title: Blacksmith
blacksmith.summary: A smith forging iron fittings and shoeing draught horses at a forge.

shipwright.title: Shipwright
shipwright.summary: A skilled shipbuilder constructing and repairing timber and iron hulls in dry docks.

ship carpenter.title: Ship Carpenter
ship carpenter.summary: A marine woodworker repairing ship decks, spars, bulkheads, and cargo hatches.

rigger.title: Rigger
rigger.summary: A dockyard specialist fitting and repairing ships' masts, standing rigging, cables, and derricks.

hobbler.title: Hobbler
hobbler.summary: A casual river or dockside boatman who helped moor, unmoor, and guide vessels in Newport's tidal waters.

plumber.title: Plumber
plumber.summary: A tradesman working with lead and iron piping for water supply, drainage, and roof flashing.

gasfitter.title: Gasfitter
gasfitter.summary: A technician installing and servicing town-gas piping, wall brackets, and street or house lamps.

insurance agent.title: Insurance Agent
insurance agent.summary: A door-to-door collector and salesman for life, burial, and industrial insurance societies.

police.title: Police
police.summary: A constable or officer of the Newport Borough or Monmouthshire Constabulary.

policeman.title: Policeman
policeman.summary: A uniformed police constable patrolling the borough streets and docks.

draper.title: Draper
draper.summary: A merchant selling woven cloth, linen, ribbons, haberdashery, and ready-made garments.

outfitter.title: Outfitter
outfitter.summary: A clothier selling men's suits, shirts, hats, and workwear.

dressmaker.title: Dressmaker
dressmaker.summary: A seamstress designing and sewing women's and children's dresses to measure.

pilot.title: Pilot
pilot.summary: A licensed navigator guiding ships safely through the tricky tides and mudflats of the Bristol Channel and River Usk.

pilotsman.title: Pilotsman
pilotsman.summary: A crewman aboard a Bristol Channel pilot cutter assisting licensed river pilots.

sawyer.title: Sawyer
sawyer.summary: A timber-yard worker sawing logs into planks and pitprops by hand-pit or steam sawmill.

postman.title: Postman
postman.summary: A uniformed Post Office letter-carrier delivering mail across Newport's street beats.

tobacconist.title: Tobacconist
tobacconist.summary: A retailer selling pipe tobacco, cigars, snuff, cigarettes, and walking sticks.

newsagent.title: Newsagent
newsagent.summary: A shopkeeper selling daily newspapers, periodicals, stationery, and often tobacco.

crane driver.title: Crane Driver
crane driver.summary: An operator of hydraulic or steam cranes hoisting coal, ore, and cargo at Newport's docks.

driver.title: Driver
driver.summary: An operator of a horse-drawn cab, delivery van, tramcar, or motor vehicle.

printer.title: Printer
printer.summary: A letterpress or lithographic tradesman printing newspapers, directories, handbills, and ledgers.

compositor.title: Compositor
compositor.summary: A printing-house craftsman setting individual metal type by hand into pages for the press.

solicitor.title: Solicitor
solicitor.summary: A qualified legal practitioner handling property conveyancing, wills, shipping disputes, and court cases.

mechanic.title: Mechanic
mechanic.summary: A skilled workshop craftsman building and repairing machinery, tools, and engines.

warehouseman.title: Warehouseman
warehouseman.summary: A worker receiving, storing, and despatching wholesale stock in a commercial warehouse.

steward.title: Steward
steward.summary: A ship's catering officer or a manager of a working-men's club or estate.

machinist.title: Machinist
machinist.summary: An operator of power-driven workshop lathes, drills, or industrial sewing machines.

boatman.title: Boatman
boatman.summary: A river or dock waterman ferrying crews, mooring lines, and small cargo on the River Usk.

caretaker.title: Caretaker
caretaker.summary: A resident custodian looking after a school, chapel, office building, or club.

saddler.title: Saddler
saddler.summary: A leatherworker making and repairing horse collars, harnesses, and saddles for hauliers and riders.

hoistman.title: Hoistman
hoistman.summary: A dockside operator controlling hydraulic coal hoists that tipped whole railway wagons into ships' holds.

dealer.title: Dealer
dealer.summary: A trader buying and selling livestock, furniture, marine stores, or general merchandise.

milkman.title: Milkman
milkman.summary: A roundsman delivering fresh milk from churns to households each morning.

dairyman.title: Dairyman
dairyman.summary: A retailer and producer selling milk, butter, cream, and eggs from a town dairy.

watchmaker.title: Watchmaker
watchmaker.summary: A precision craftsman assembling, regulating, and repairing pocket watches and clocks.

wheelwright.title: Wheelwright
wheelwright.summary: A specialist wood-and-iron craftsman building and repairing spoked wooden wheels for carts and wagons.

salesman.title: Salesman
salesman.summary: A wholesale or retail shop assistant selling goods to customers.

accountant.title: Accountant
accountant.summary: A financial specialist auditing books, preparing balance sheets, and advising businesses.

hawker.title: Hawker
hawker.summary: An itinerant street seller crying fruit, fish, firewood, or household wares from a barrow.

inspector.title: Inspector
inspector.summary: A senior official inspecting railway lines, tramways, sanitation, schools, or police beats.

electrician.title: Electrician
electrician.summary: A technician installing early electric lighting, tramway wiring, bells, and industrial motors.

justice of the peace.title: Justice of the Peace
justice of the peace.summary: An unpaid local magistrate (J.P.) presiding over Newport's summary petty-sessions courts.

storekeeper.title: Storekeeper
storekeeper.summary: An employee managing tools, spare parts, and supplies in a railway, dock, or factory store.

roller.title: Roller
roller.summary: A senior iron- or steelworks craftsman passing glowing ingots through heavy rollers to make bars, rails, or sheets.

shearer.title: Shearer
shearer.summary: A mill worker operating heavy mechanical shears to trim rolled iron or steel plates to size.

puddler.title: Puddler
puddler.summary: A skilled ironworks furnaceman stirring molten pig iron with long rods to burn off carbon and produce wrought iron.

furnaceman.title: Furnaceman
furnaceman.summary: A heavy-industry worker charging and tending blast, puddling, or reheating furnaces.

patternmaker.title: Patternmaker
patternmaker.summary: A master woodworker carving exact wooden patterns from which foundry sand moulds were made for iron castings.

tinsmith.title: Tinsmith
tinsmith.summary: A metalworker shaping tinplate and sheet iron into cans, lanterns, kettles, and roof gutters.

timekeeper.title: Timekeeper
timekeeper.summary: A works clerk recording workers' arrival, departure, and piecework hours for weekly wages.

weighman.title: Weighman
weighman.summary: An official operating weighbridges to record the tonnage of coal wagons, ships' cargo, or iron.

checker.title: Checker
checker.summary: A dock or railway tallyman checking loaded goods and timber against bills of lading.

miller.title: Miller
miller.summary: A worker grinding wheat and grain into flour at Newport's steam or water mills.

upholsterer.title: Upholsterer
upholsterer.summary: A craftsman stuffing, springing, and covering chairs, sofas, and carriage seats.

cab proprietor.title: Cab Proprietor
cab proprietor.summary: An owner of horse-drawn hansoms or motor cabs hired out for street fares.

cabman.title: Cabman
cabman.summary: A driver of a licensed horse-drawn cab plying for hire at stations and cab ranks.

coachman.title: Coachman
coachman.summary: A private or livery driver handling horse-drawn carriages.

packer.title: Packer
packer.summary: A worker crating glass, tinplate, or warehouse goods for rail and sea shipment.

chemist.title: Chemist
chemist.summary: A qualified dispensing pharmacist compounding medicines and selling toiletries and photographic supplies.

surgeon.title: Surgeon
surgeon.summary: A qualified medical doctor practising surgery and general medicine.

physician and surgeon.title: Physician and Surgeon
physician and surgeon.summary: A fully qualified general medical practitioner treating both medical and surgical cases.

stevedore.title: Stevedore
stevedore.summary: A specialist dockworker stowing and securing heavy cargo inside ocean-going ships' holds.

dockman.title: Dockman
dockman.summary: A general dock employee working lock gates, quaysides, and cargo sheds.

docker.title: Docker
docker.summary: A quayside worker loading and discharging cargo vessels at Newport Docks.

ironmonger.title: Ironmonger
ironmonger.summary: A hardware retailer selling nails, locks, tools, grates, and domestic metalware.

sailmaker.title: Sailmaker
sailmaker.summary: A marine craftsman cutting and hand-stitching heavy canvas sails, awnings, and hatch tarpaulins.

boarding house.title: Boarding House
boarding house.summary: Lodgings providing rooms and meals for visiting sailors, commercial travellers, and workers.

ostler.title: Ostler
ostler.summary: A stableman grooming, feeding, and harnessing horses at an inn, coaching yard, or haulier's stables.

cellarman.title: Cellarman
cellarman.summary: A worker tapping, fining, and storing beer casks and wine bottles in a hotel, pub, or wine merchant's cellar.

jeweller.title: Jeweller
jeweller.summary: A retailer and craftsman dealing in gold and silver jewellery, watches, and plate.

photographer.title: Photographer
photographer.summary: A studio operator taking glass-plate portraits and topographical views.

teacher.title: Teacher
teacher.summary: A schoolmaster or schoolmistress teaching at one of Newport's board, voluntary, or grammar schools.

musician.title: Musician
musician.summary: A professional instrumentalist or music teacher performing in theatres, bands, and parlours.

florist.title: Florist
florist.summary: A retailer and grower arranging cut flowers, wreaths, and garden plants.

watchman.title: Watchman
watchman.summary: A night guard patrolling docks, timber yards, factories, or municipal works.

quarryman.title: Quarryman
quarryman.summary: A worker blasting and splitting stone from local quarries for road metal and building.

fish bar.title: Fish Bar
fish bar.summary: A shop or counter selling fresh fish or fried fish and chips.

cooper.title: Cooper
cooper.summary: A craftsman making and hooping watertight wooden barrels, casks, and tubs.

architect.title: Architect
architect.summary: A professional designer of residential terraces, chapels, civic halls, and commercial buildings.

charwoman.title: Charwoman
charwoman.summary: A woman hired by the day to scrub, clean, and launder for households or offices.

p.o..title: P.O. (Post Office)
p.o..summary: An employee of the General Post Office, such as a telegraphist, sorter, or sub-postmaster.

refreshments.title: Refreshments
refreshments.summary: A tea room, temperance café, or dining stall serving light meals and non-alcoholic drinks.

boiler coverer.title: Boiler Coverer
boiler coverer.summary: An industrial insulator lagging steam boilers and pipes with asbestos or felt to retain heat.

wagon repairer.title: Wagon Repairer
wagon repairer.summary: A tradesman mending wooden and iron coal wagons in railway or private sidings.

wagon examiner.title: Wagon Examiner
wagon examiner.summary: A railway inspector checking wagon wheels, axles, and brakes before trains departed.

lamplighter.title: Lamplighter
lamplighter.summary: A municipal worker lighting and extinguishing Newport's street gas lamps at dusk and dawn.

berthing master.title: Berthing Master
berthing master.summary: A dock official directing ships to their assigned quayside berths and overseeing lock movements.
